READ THE LAUREATE

Monetary policy after money targeting

Interest and Prices: Foundations of a Theory of Monetary Policy · Michael Woodford

Woodford rebuilds monetary-policy analysis around interest-rate decisions, expectations and explicit rules, explaining how a central bank can stabilise prices and economic activity without targeting a monetary aggregate.

01

Expectations move the economy

What households and firms expect about future policy changes current spending, pricing and inflation.

02

Rules improve credibility

Systematic interest-rate responses can anchor inflation expectations better than improvised decisions.

03

Policy has a welfare test

Price stability and output stability are evaluated together through the distortions policy can reduce.

Publisher catalogue page ↗

WHY IT MATTERS

Make policy models answer to individual decisions

Hall and Woodford helped rebuild macroeconomic stabilisation on the choices and expectations of households and firms. Their work strengthened the New Keynesian framework used to study how monetary and fiscal policy can reduce swings in output and inflation.
